Thanks again for the call this morning — great context on FintechCo's latency and data residency needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get you a clean, apples-to-apples comparison vs the hyperscalers.

Recap (what you told us):
- Primary regions: US (east/west), EU (Ireland), APAC (Singapore).
- Target p95 latency: <=100ms (US/EU), <=200ms (APAC) for your 256-token generation workload.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain within EU region for certain product flows.
- Security: SOC 2 + SSO + audit logs required for procurement.

Proposed evaluation plan:
1) Multi-region latency pings + synthetic generation runs (redwood hosted endpoints in us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1).
2) Throughput/cost comparison (tokens/sec and $/1M tokens) vs AWS Bedrock and GCP Vertex using identical prompt sets.
3) Quality check on your top-10 prompts (regression testing vs current provider).
4) Validation of data residency controls (Private deployment vs regional routing) and documentation for procurement.

Attachments: I attached a mutual action plan (MAP) that maps milestones to owners.

Ask/next steps:
- Can your infra/SRE run the synthetic latency script Marissa will share? We ask for 50 requests per region, capturing p50/p95/p99.
- Can we schedule a 45-min SE call (Marissa + Dev) this week to walk through the test harness and any sample payloads?

I'll coordinate timing once I get your availability. Happy to include Jordan on the exec check-in if/when we surface procurement questions.

Thanks,
Sean

Hi Chris / Samira —
Attaching a short test plan and sample curl commands you can run from each region. No auth complexity — use the read-only test token I sent in our shared secure link.

Top-level instructions:
1) Run 50 sequential requests from a host in each target region (US-East, EU-West, APAC-SG). Capture p50, p95, p99, and mean.
2) Run a small concurrent test (50 concurrency, 120 threads total) to approximate burst behavior and report failures/timeouts.
3) For throughput/cost: we will run a 10k-token steady-state generation on our side with and without batching to report tokens/sec and $/1M tokens.

Sample curl (replace <REGION-ENDPOINT> and <TOKEN>):

curl -X POST "https://<REGION-ENDPOINT>/v1/generate"
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rw-medium-0610","input":"<your-sample-prompt>","max_tokens":256}'

Notes:
- Endpoints we will provision for this test: us-east-1.redwood.ai, eu-west-1.redwood.ai, asia-southeast1.redwood.ai
- If you need a script, we can drop a small python harness into a shared GCS/Drive link.

I'll also drop a short checklist for verification of data residency and for procurement (SOC 2 link, SSO docs).

Thanks — Marissa

Quick competitive notes / what we'll surface in the report:
- Redwood differentiators vs hyperscalers: dedicated capacity (predictable p95), prefix/KV cache (low-cost repeated prompt patterns), quantization-friendly runtime yielding lower GPU footprint in many cases, and private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for strict data residency.
- Hyperscalers (AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex): strong global infra footprint and deep integrations, but often higher per-token unit cost and less transparent kernel-level latencies for generation workloads.
- Anthropic / other inference APIs: competitive in quality for some workloads; may lack regional private deployment options and enterprise routing/fallback controls we provide.

Recommended additional tests:
1) Model parity check: run your top-10 prompts across rw-medium-0610 (Redwood) and the equivalent Bedrock/GVertex model to check for output drift.
2) Quantization + perf: test a quantized variant (if acceptable for quality) to measure cost improvement.
3) Routing failover: simulate region failure and measure fallback latency to a secondary region (Redwood can route by policy).

I'll prepare a short CSV with per-region p95/p99 expected baselines and attach it to the follow-up.

—Dev
